landmarks.name: Tait McKenzie Centre
facts: It hosted basketball and volleyball at the 2017 North American Indigenous Games.
It is named after a renowned sculptor, doctor, soldier and physical educator.

landmarks.name: Ignat Kaneff Building - Osgoode Hall Law School
facts: It is home to the Law Commission of Ontario.
It was designed by architect Jack Diamond; construction began in the summer of 2009.

landmarks.name: Vanier College
facts: It is self-governed day to day by a master, the master's office and students.
Founded in 1966, it is the second-oldest residential college on the Keele campus.

landmarks.name: Sobeys Stadium
facts: It is a tennis stadium that hosts the Canadian Open, alternating men's and women's events with Montreal.

landmarks.name: Ross Building
facts: It is named after the university's first president, like a parkway and a valedictorian award.
A ramp leading up to it was demolished when Vari Hall was built, by 1989.

landmarks.name: York Lanes
facts: It is a two-storey indoor mall on the Keele campus.

landmarks.name: Seymour Schulich Building
facts: The subway station opened directly across from its main entrance in December 2017.
It opened in August 2003 at a cost of $102 million.

landmarks.name: Vari Hall
facts: It is mostly lecture halls, designed by Raymond Moriyama to give the campus a new face.
It was built in the early 1990s.

landmarks.name: Scott Library
facts: The Sound and Moving Images Library, with the audiovisual collection, is on its first floor.

landmarks.name: Second Student Centre
facts: It was purpose-built after students voted for it in an October 2013 referendum.

landmarks.name: Health, Nursing and Environmental Studies
facts: It was built as a joint venture between two faculties and is known as HNE.

landmarks.name: Bergeron Centre for Engineering Excellence
facts: It officially opened on April 8, 2016, after a $10 million gift, then the largest ever from an alumnus.

landmarks.name: Bennett Centre for Student Services
facts: It was renamed in 2006 to recognise a supporter of the university.

landmarks.name: Rob and Cheryl McEwen Graduate Study and Research Building
First Student Centre
facts: It is the original of the two student centre buildings.

landmarks.name: McLaughlin College
facts: It is a residential college named after an automaker.
It opened in 1968.

landmarks.name: The Joan and Martin Goldfarb Gallery of York University
Vanier Residence
facts: Its residence life team of dons, porters and programmers is all upper-year students.
